message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the federal “long‑weekend” holidays in Canada for 2023.  
(If you’re looking at a specific province or territory, keep in mind that some holidays—like Family Day, Civic Holiday, or provincial holidays such as St. Patricks’ Day in Ontario—might shift the exact dates.)

| Holiday | Date in 2023 | Observed (if shifted) | Typical long‑weekend span |
|---------|--------------|-----------------------|---------------------------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Jan 1 (Sunday) | Observed on Mon Jan 2 | Jan 1–3 (New Year’s Day observed on Jan 2) |
| **Family Day** (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, etc.) | Feb 20 (Monday) | — | Feb 18–20 |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 (Friday) | — | Apr 7–9 |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 (Monday) | — | May 20–22 |
| **Canada Day** | Jul 1 (Saturday) | Observed on Mon Jul 3 | Jul 1–3 (Canada Day observed on Jul 3) |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 (Monday) | — | Sep 2–4 |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 (Monday) | — | Oct 7–9 |
| **Remembrance Day** | Nov 11 (Saturday) | Observed on Mon Nov 13 | Nov 11–13 (Remembrance Day observed on Nov 13) |
| **Christmas Day** | Dec 25 (Monday) | — | Dec 23–25 |
| **Boxing Day** | Dec 26 (Tuesday) | — | Dec 24–26 |

### Quick notes

* **Observed dates**: When a holiday falls on a weekend, the federal government usually observes it on the following Monday. That’s why Canada Day (Jul 1) and New Year’s Day (Jan 1) are observed on the next working day in 2023.
* **Provincial variations**: Some provinces have extra holidays (e.g., St. Patricks’ Day in Ontario, Civic Holiday in most provinces, etc.). Those will create additional long weekends that aren’t listed here.
* **Planning tip**: If you’re building an app, consider pulling from a reliable holiday API (e.g., Calendarific, Timezonedb, or a local government API) to keep the data up‑to‑date and province‑specific.

Let me know if you’d like the same info broken out by province or if you need help integrating it into your app!
